title: Vowel Spellchecker
summary: Given a wordlist, create a spellchecker that corrects a query word by matching it to a wordlist entry (case-insensitive) and returning the matched word with the original case.
statement: Given a wordlist, create a spellchecker that corrects a query word by matching it to a wordlist entry (case-insensitive) and returning the matched word with the original case.
constraints: Words contain only English letters and have length one through seven.
Apply matching precedence: exact case, then first case-insensitive match, then first vowel-normalized match.
Treat a, e, i, o, and u as interchangeable only in the third matching stage; return an empty string when no rule matches.
hints: Matching precedence matters as much as normalization.
Store the first word for each lowercase key and each vowel-masked lowercase key.
Check the exact set, lowercase map, and vowel map in that order for each query.
First-write maps preserve wordlist priority, and the three ordered lookups exactly implement the specification.
editorial: First-write maps preserve wordlist priority, and the three ordered lookups exactly implement the specification.

tests.explanation: Exact case wins first; otherwise the first case-insensitive or vowel-normalized match is returned.
Ignoring capitalization matches the sole dictionary word yellow.
